subject.title: Feature request: first-class async result routing back to originating topic sessions

question: Should OpenClaw create a core-owned async callback route registry, expose missing plugin/API primitives so this lives outside core, or defer the feature behind existing wake/hooks/cron building blocks?
rationale: The remaining work is not a localized bug fix; it requires product ownership over storage, privacy, safety policy, event-source matching, ambiguity handling, and core-versus-plugin boundaries.

options.title: Design plugin/API contract first
options.body: Keep core lean by identifying any missing extension points, then let route registries and source watchers live as plugins or ClawHub packages unless a small core primitive is clearly required.

options.title: Build a minimal core registry
options.body: Accept core ownership of a local single-gateway route ledger, matcher, dedupe state, and safe action runner with migration and privacy policy tests.

options.title: Defer to existing primitives
options.body: Document current targeted wake, hooks, cron, delivery-context, and approval building blocks and leave higher-level callback routing to workspace-specific implementations for now.

recommendation.title: Design plugin/API contract first
recommendation.body: Keep core lean by identifying any missing extension points, then let route registries and source watchers live as plugins or ClawHub packages unless a small core primitive is clearly required.

likelyOwner.reason: The question is primarily product/API scope, and Peter Steinberger appears in current main and adjacent wake-routing history while VISION.md provides the relevant boundary guidance.
